_comment: Skill Repo Spec v1 s9 -- every path in this repo belongs to exactly one class.
TOOL    = code, SKILL.md, docs, reference data, and metrics ABOUT THE SKILL. Public.
FIXTURE = LIFELIKE test data: rows that look like real records, whose real version is
sitting right there in the operator's life and is structurally indistinguishable.
Must be produced by tools/make_fixtures.py -- a real record cannot be regenerated,
so pasting one in fails at commit. (A self-evidently fake canary or an Acme mock is
NOT lifelike and does not need a generator; the risk it guards against is a person
reaching for a convenient REAL example, and there is no temptation to reach for a
real value that would look obviously wrong next to FAKE_CANARY_XYZ.)
DATA    = anything a REAL RUN produced. Never git-tracked. Lives in the private companion
config, resolved at runtime by tools/datadir.py. This repo ships only the schema.
data_sealed = a path that HELD real data, was purged, and must stay dead.
Enforced by tools/data_boundary.py in .githooks and in CI.
`tool` is not a fourth class. It is the per-path allowlist for check 4, which fails any tracked
file that WEARS the shape of real-run output. TOOL is the default class and needs no entry --
except where a hand-written file is shaped like a ledger, which has to be argued for in the diff.
_tool_note: Hand-cut replay inputs for the signal-yield engine (test_yield.py, test_yield_temporal.py), 19 lines total, ids op-a/op-b and a deliberately dead handle. They carry the LIVE LEDGER's filenames because the reader resolves an archive dir by name, so the test cannot exercise the real path under any other name -- which is exactly why they are enumerated rather than exempted by directory: the name stays usable for tests and unusable for a record. They are not declared `fixture` because this repo has no tools/make_fixtures.py and check 2 would then fail on a missing generator; if one is ever written, move these two lines from `tool` to `fixture` and let byte-equality take over.
_audited: 2026-07-31 RE-AUDIT (supersedes the 2026-07-13 sweep, which recorded an empty declaration for this repo). The earlier sweep asked only whether shipped code appends to a TRACKED file here. That question is too narrow: it clears every path that is gitignored, and .gitignore is advisory -- `git add -f` walks straight through it, which is the whole reason declarations exist. This pass asked instead whether shipped code or shipped docs can put REAL-RUN OUTPUT at a repo-relative path at all. ANSWER: it produces a great deal of real-run output -- the opportunity ledger, the pulls denominator log, dedup state, daily digests -- and every byte lands in the PRIVATE companion repo, which is the decided shape and not a problem. archive.py's resolve_archive_dir() goes explicit-arg, then find_config_dir() ($DAILY_HOTSPOTS_CONFIG, then the dotfile fallbacks), then ~/.daily-hotspots-config/archive: no DEFAULT branch returns a path in this repo, though the explicit-arg branch will hand back whatever a caller passes, so this is a statement about where output goes unattended, not a statement about where it CAN go. watchlist.json is gitignored here but it is a user INPUT read from the config dir, not output. Nothing to declare. What DID change on 2026-07-31 is that the out-of-band boundary check can finally SEE this skill: tools/datadir.py now follows $DAILY_HOTSPOTS_CONFIG, so the check reports where the ledger actually lives instead of reporting not-initialized over a ledger that grows every day.
_armed: 2026-07-31 ARMED. The empty declaration above stopped being the control on this date. An independent verifier cloned this repo, committed metrics/live-runs.jsonl and runs/transcript.json into it, and tools/data_boundary.py exited 0: checks 1..3 only ever inspect what the manifest DECLARES, so a manifest that declares nothing was enforcing nothing, and the careful paragraph above was doing the work a check is supposed to do. Check 4 now runs off the TRACKED FILE LIST instead and fails any file wearing the shape of real-run output (a jsonl under metrics/, a runs/ tree, a dated file under an output dir, a live-ledger filename, a database) whether or not this manifest declares a thing. So the empty `data` list is a claim re-tested on every commit and in CI, not a note taken on faith. That distinction is load-bearing here: resolve_archive_dir() defaults outside this repo but returns an explicit --archive-dir verbatim, so 'the default resolver points elsewhere' was never the same statement as 'nothing can land here'.
_data_home: ~/.daily-hotspots-config/data/   (override with $DAILY_HOTSPOTS_DATA_DIR). If this skill ever needs to record real-run output, it goes THERE -- never back into this repo.
